newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - June 24.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - June 24.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The People's Initiative for Reform, Modernisation and Action yesterday presented to the Commission on Elections 5.5 million signatures of people who allegedly favour the lifting of term limits on the President and other officials. (ALL NEWSPAPERS)

- At least 20 people were killed over the weekend when government troopers launched one of their fiercest offensives against the Moro Islamic Liberation Front (MILF), whose members are believed to be engaged in kidnapping in Mindanao. (STAR)

- President Fidel Ramos and Greek President Constantinos Stephanopoulos agreed yesterday in Athens to identify and explore areas for more active economic cooperation between the Philippines and Greece. (BULLETIN/JOURNAL)
- North Negros Marketing Corp, a unit of cash-strapped Victorias Milling Co Inc, is seeking suspension of payments for its 1.86 billion pesos worth of debts. (ALL NEWSPAPERS)

- Petron's fuel production will drop by 10,000 barrels daily for a month as a result of the breakdown last Friday of its catalytic reformer, an equipment used to process gasoline and other petroleum products. (ALL NEWSPAPERS)

- Treasury bill rates went up across the board by almost half a percentage point as an offshoot of last week's decision of the Central Bank to jack up its overnight borrowing rate to defend the peso against speculative attack. (ALL NEWSPAPERS)
